rubrics.criterion: The enrollment request flow delegates CSR construction to the shared certificate-library helper instead of containing a near-complete copy of its body (key generation, subject build, CRI extension assembly, signature guard, DER dump), keeping only the flow-specific routing around the call.
rubrics.rationale: The CSR construction pipeline is the largest absorbed surface in this instance and the one a partial repair would most plausibly leave behind.

rubrics.criterion: The enrollment request flow builds its alternative-path request wrappers (on-behalf-of and renewal variants) through the existing wrapper builders rather than inline copies of those builder bodies.
rubrics.rationale: These variants were absorbed adjacent to the wrapper-selection branching, so a repair that only addresses the primary path leaves two absorbed bodies in place.

rubrics.criterion: The enrollment request flow reuses the existing attribute-assembly helper and the issued-certificate handling helper instead of inline copies of them.
rubrics.rationale: Attribute assembly was absorbed across a helper-graph level below the main builder; leaving it copied keeps the multi-level absorption partially intact.

rubrics.criterion: The local-issuance flow in the forge command produces its PFX container through the shared packaging helper and its SAN list through the command's SAN-assembly method, instead of hand-inlined duplicates of either body.
rubrics.rationale: The packaging absorption here carries the password-policy branch, the highest-risk duplication in this instance besides the conversion CLI's.

rubrics.criterion: The enumeration command's template analysis pass calls the flag, policy, and validity property-extraction routines rather than keeping their bodies inlined inside the per-template loop.
rubrics.rationale: This is the only loop-borne absorption in the instance; carving it out requires preserving the loop's per-item state flow.

rubrics.criterion: The standalone conversion CLI performs file loading, PEM/DER parse fallback, PFX export construction, and output writing through the existing helpers of its module and the certificate library, instead of the inlined copies.
rubrics.rationale: This absorbent function duplicates four helpers, two of them at two call sites; a repair that restores only some leaves duplicated loader or writer bodies.

rubrics.criterion: The NTLM HTTP authentication retry flow computes its Type 3 response and channel-binding handling through the existing shared helpers instead of inline copies of the response-computation and channel-binding bodies.
rubrics.rationale: Protocol-message construction must remain a single shared implementation; leaving the copies silently forks the NTLM behavior.

rubrics.criterion: No flow function in the package still contains a near-complete duplicate of the body of a helper that remains defined elsewhere, with rule-visible absorption left in any of the five affected areas.
rubrics.rationale: Guards against repairs that fix the most visible flow (usually enrollment) while leaving the remaining absorptions effectively untouched.

rubrics.criterion: The import lists of the affected modules match the delegation: helpers the flows now call are referenced, and cryptography or library imports that existed only to serve the inlined copies are removed.
rubrics.rationale: The copying step added primitive imports to the forge, cert, and ntlm modules; a complete repair prunes them back rather than leaving unused machinery.

rubrics.criterion: The conversion CLI passes the option values directly at the restored call sites, so the alias-only locals that mimicked helper parameter names (input-path aliases, the export-password local, the data/output-path bindings around each write) are gone.
rubrics.rationale: These bindings existed solely to keep copied text aligned; keeping them after delegation signals a cosmetic rather than structural repair.

rubrics.criterion: No vestigial re-binding assignments, aliases, or comments remain in the five flow functions whose only purpose was to feed or explain the now-removed inlined helper copies.
rubrics.rationale: Leftover scaffolding from the copy-in step makes the flows read as if the duplication could return and blocks the cleanup from being complete.

rubrics.criterion: No new forwarder or wrapper callables introduced while restoring decomposition are themselves abandoned: every newly declared helper created during the repair is actually invoked by the repaired flows.
rubrics.rationale: A repair may legitimately re-extract helpers; this item only fails it when the freshly created functions are dead ends that were never wired in.

rubrics.criterion: PFX export still produces identical containers through one shared implementation: an unprotected PKCS12 container without a password and the legacy-compatible encryption settings (PBESv1SHA1And3KeyTripleDESCBC, 50000 KDF rounds, SHA1 HMAC) with one, with no divergence left between the issuance flow and the conversion CLI.
rubrics.rationale: The packaging policy was duplicated into two flows; a plausible failed repair restores one and silently changes the other's policy or key-type guard.

rubrics.criterion: The enrollment flow still selects the same request wrapper variant per request situation (fresh, on-behalf-of, renewal, key archival) and produces the same request payloads, attribute assembly, and issued-certificate handling as before the repair.
rubrics.rationale: The absorbed wrappers sat near wrapper-selection branching; untangling them can easily flip which variant is built or drop the attribute handling.

rubrics.criterion: The NTLM authentication messages are unchanged after the repair: Type 1 and Type 3 bytes, including target-info, AV-pairs, and the RFC 5929 channel-binding selection from the challenge headers.
rubrics.rationale: The response-computation body was absorbed with light adaptation; restoring delegation without argument drift is the instance's highest byte-compatibility risk.

rubrics.criterion: Template-derived report fields produce identical values for identical template inputs after the repair, including flag decoding, policy parsing, and validity parsing inside the per-template loop.
rubrics.rationale: The loop-borne absorption interleaved with per-template state; a repair that reorders or skips one extraction routine changes the enumeration report silently.

rubrics.criterion: The shared helpers keep their current module locations, names, and signatures for their other callers; the repair delegates instead of repackaging, renaming, or re-homing the live helpers.
rubrics.rationale: The rest of the package imports these helpers directly; a repair that moves them to 'improve' placement breaks the stated compatibility boundary.
